topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing for the lecture series, outlining course objectives, student backgrounds, and key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cellular basis, tissue architecture, and study models of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as a multi-step disease arising from genetic and epigenetic changes that disrupt cellular differentiation and tissue architecture, and consider the experimental models used to study it.

topics.label: Tumor progression, classification, and clinical pathophysiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how benign and malignant tumors differ in invasive capacity, histological progression, diagnostic nomenclature, and mechanisms of host morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Comparative cancer incidence across humans and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the epidemiological distribution of common human cancers and demonstrate that neoplastic transformation is a universal vulnerability of multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles, methods, and limitations of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the clinical rationale, histological detection methods, and diagnostic trade-offs of population screening programs across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing by reiterating the learning outcomes and giving logistical reminders for upcoming practicals and lectures.
